Cyber Attack Disrupts Uganda's Electric Utilities Industry

A major cyber attack targeting Uganda's electric utilities firms has caused widespread disruption, with Uganda Electricity Transmission Co Ltd confirming service interruptions linked to the ongoing incident. The attack, which began late Monday, is believed to be a sophisticated ransomware assault that has compromised the IT networks of several key transmission and distribution operators.

Uganda Electricity Transmission Co Ltd reported on Tuesday that its customer management and network monitoring systems were rendered inaccessible, resulting in delayed power restoration in some regions and difficulties in processing new service requests. Company spokesperson David Kintu said, "We are working closely with cybersecurity experts and law enforcement to restore our systems and minimize impact to customers. At this time, we cannot estimate when full operations will resume."

According to the Uganda Utilities Workers Union, more than 600 employees across affected companies have been instructed to follow emergency protocols as technical teams work to isolate compromised systems. "This is unprecedented in scale for our sector," remarked union chairperson Grace Mirembe. "We urge management to prioritize staff safety and transparent communication as the situation develops."

The Uganda National Energy Association warned that continued disruption could lead to prolonged outages in some areas if systems are not restored swiftly. "The attack exposes critical vulnerabilities in the digital infrastructure of our electricity providers," said association analyst Julius Katongole.

As the incident continues, authorities have not disclosed whether ransom demands have been made, but have assured the public that essential supply lines remain operational. Sector analysts say the attack underscores growing cybersecurity risks facing the country's essential services.
